newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AGL share limit seen lifted soon - expert.
newsitem.headline: AGL share limit seen lifted soon - expert.

text.p: The current five percent shareholding restriction placed on the stock of Australia Gas Light Co (AGL) was of historical relevance only and was likely to be removed within 12 months, a corporate finance executive said on Wednesday.

"Our expectation is that in New South Wales the AGL shareholder cap of five percent will probably be legislated out within the next 12 months," Alan James, joint divisional head corporate finance for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell told a gas conference here.

James said the shareholder limit on a number of Australia utilities, including AGL, Santos Ltd and Queensland's Allgas Energy, appeared to be inconsistent with deregulation and the current restructure of the wholesale gas market in Australia.
"What that will mean for AGL is quite interesting. AGL as a takeover target looks very attractive to a number of companies," James said.
He said AGL was likely to be trying to manage the process of the shareholder restriction being lifted, which would require a change in legislation by the New South Wales state government.
He said the removal of ownership restrictions of Allgas and Santos was less predictable.
AGL shares were four cents firmer at A$7.99 at 12.40 p.m. (0240 GMT), while Allgas shares were steady at A$13.60 and Santos was three cents lower at A$5.51.
